note: Subjects/9701 Chemistry/13 An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry/13.3 Shapes of organic molecules; σ and π bonds.md
outline: Organic carbon skeletons may be straight-chained, branched or cyclic. Classify each atom locally: sp³ carbon is tetrahedral with bond angles near 109.5°, sp² carbon is trigonal planar with angles near 120°, and sp carbon is linear with a 180° angle. A single bond is σ; a double bond has one σ and one π; a triple bond has one σ and two π. σ bonds arise from end-on overlap, while π bonds arise from sideways overlap of unhybridised p orbitals. Planar means that the atoms lie in the same plane: all ethene atoms do, whereas a saturated six-membered ring is usually non-planar.

misconceptions.statement: A bent drawing of a carbon chain makes it branched.
misconceptions.refutation: A straight chain may zigzag; branching means a carbon is bonded to a side carbon chain.
misconceptions.contrast: Trace the carbon connectivity rather than the shape of the drawing.

misconceptions.statement: Every atom in a double-bonded molecule is sp² hybridised.
misconceptions.refutation: Only the atoms involved in the double bond are necessarily sp²; an adjacent saturated carbon remains sp³.
misconceptions.contrast: Classify each atom separately from its local bonding.

misconceptions.statement: A double bond consists of two σ bonds.
misconceptions.refutation: A double bond has one σ bond from end-on overlap and one π bond from sideways p-orbital overlap.
misconceptions.contrast: Count one σ for every connected atom pair and one additional π for each double bond.

misconceptions.statement: A cyclic molecule must be planar.
misconceptions.refutation: A saturated six-membered carbon ring has sp³ carbon centres and generally adopts a non-planar conformation.
misconceptions.contrast: Check local hybridisation and three-dimensional arrangement, not only whether a ring is drawn flat.

misconceptions.statement: Planar ethene means only its two carbon atoms lie in a plane.
misconceptions.refutation: All six nuclei in ethene lie in the same plane; each carbon has trigonal planar local geometry.
misconceptions.contrast: Planar describes the arrangement of all atoms being discussed.

flashcards.front: Describe straight-chained, branched and cyclic carbon skeletons.
flashcards.back: Straight-chained: one unbranched carbon chain; branched: a side chain attached to the main chain; cyclic: a closed ring of atoms.

flashcards.front: Describe σ and π bonding in a C=C double bond.
flashcards.back: One σ bond from end-on overlap and one π bond from sideways overlap of unhybridised p orbitals.

9701-13.3.1.motivate: Two molecules can contain the same number of carbon atoms yet connect them in a chain, a side chain, or a ring. Tracing connectivity helps you recognise the carbon skeleton before discussing shape or reactions.
9701-13.3.1.establish: Describe an organic molecule as straight-chained when its carbon atoms form one unbranched open chain; the chain may be drawn as a zigzag. Describe it as branched when a carbon side chain is attached to a main carbon chain. Describe it as cyclic when its atoms form a closed ring. Butane is straight-chained, 2-methylpropane is branched, and cyclohexane is cyclic. These labels are about which atoms are joined, not the visual straightness of lines in a diagram.
9701-13.3.1.connect: Use the structural or skeletal formula you already know: follow every carbon end and vertex. You will then be able to separate connectivity from the three-dimensional shape at each carbon.
9701-13.3.1.note:
- Straight-chained: one unbranched open carbon chain.
- Branched: a carbon side chain attached to the main chain.
- Cyclic: a closed ring of atoms.
- A zigzag drawing can still show a straight chain.
9701-13.3.1.self_explain: Why can a zigzag skeletal formula still represent a straight-chained molecule?

discover.stem: Which feature makes a carbon skeleton branched?

options.A: A bend in a drawn bond
options.B: A side carbon chain attached to the main chain

discover.explanation: Branching is a connection in the carbon skeleton; bends in a drawing do not create branches.

9701-13.3.2.motivate: The angles around carbon control how an organic molecule occupies space. A single molecule can contain different carbon shapes, so classify each atom locally.
9701-13.3.2.establish: Hybridisation is mixing of atomic orbitals on an atom to form orbitals used in σ bonding. Four σ-bond directions at an $sp^3$ carbon produce a tetrahedral arrangement with bond angles about $109.5^\circ$. Three σ-bond directions at an $sp^2$ carbon produce a trigonal planar arrangement with angles about $120^\circ$ and leave one unhybridised p orbital. Two σ-bond directions at an $sp$ carbon produce a linear arrangement with a $180^\circ$ angle and leave two unhybridised p orbitals. For example, ethane carbon is $sp^3$, ethene carbon is $sp^2$, and ethyne carbon is $sp$. The listed angles are approximate when the attached groups differ.
9701-13.3.2.connect: The electron-domain idea from VSEPR predicts the same local geometries. Hybridisation also tells you how many unhybridised p orbitals are available for π bonding.
9701-13.3.2.note:
- $sp^3$: four σ directions; tetrahedral; about $109.5^\circ$.
- $sp^2$: three σ directions; trigonal planar; about $120^\circ$.
- $sp$: two σ directions; linear; $180^\circ$.
- Classify each atom from its own bonding.
9701-13.3.2.self_explain: Why is the methyl carbon in propene tetrahedral while the two alkene carbons are trigonal planar?

discover.stem: What is the local geometry of a carbon with three σ-bond directions and one unhybridised p orbital?
discover.explanation: Three sp² orbitals form the trigonal planar σ framework; the remaining p orbital can form a π bond.

9701-13.3.3.motivate: A bond line in a structural formula can hide more than one type of orbital overlap. Separating σ and π components lets you count bonds correctly.
9701-13.3.3.establish: A σ bond forms by end-on orbital overlap along the line joining two nuclei. A π bond forms by sideways overlap of parallel unhybridised p orbitals above and below the σ framework. An $sp^3$ atom uses its hybrid orbitals for σ bonds and normally has no unhybridised p orbital for π bonding. An $sp^2$ atom uses three hybrid orbitals for σ bonds and has one p orbital for one π bond. An $sp$ atom uses two hybrid orbitals for σ bonds and has two p orbitals for two π bonds. Thus a C–C single bond contains one σ, a C=C double bond one σ plus one π, and a C≡C triple bond one σ plus two π bonds. C–H σ bonding can involve carbon hybrid-orbital overlap with hydrogen $1s$.
9701-13.3.3.connect: The hybridisation and shapes you just classified explain the remaining p orbitals. When counting, first give each connected atom pair one σ bond, then count extra π bonds from multiple bonds.
9701-13.3.3.note:
- σ: end-on overlap along the internuclear axis.
- π: sideways overlap of unhybridised p orbitals.
- Single: one σ; double: one σ and one π; triple: one σ and two π.
- $sp^2$ leaves one p orbital; $sp$ leaves two.
9701-13.3.3.self_explain: Why does a C=C double bond contain one σ bond and one π bond rather than two σ bonds?

discover.stem: How many π bonds are in one C≡C triple bond?
discover.explanation: One bond component is σ and the other two are π bonds from two pairs of p orbitals.

9701-13.3.4.motivate: Organic structures are often printed flat, but their atoms may occupy three-dimensional positions. The word planar is a claim about actual atom positions.
9701-13.3.4.establish: Planar means that the atoms being described lie in the same plane. In ethene, both carbon atoms are $sp^2$ hybridised and trigonal planar. The carbon atoms and all four hydrogen atoms lie in one plane, so the whole ethene molecule is planar. The unhybridised p orbitals are perpendicular to this plane and overlap sideways to form the π bond. Do not infer planarity solely from a flat drawing: cyclohexane has tetrahedral $sp^3$ carbon centres and normally adopts a non-planar, puckered ring. A trigonal planar group within a larger molecule need not make every atom of that molecule coplanar.
9701-13.3.4.connect: Use local shapes from hybridisation to test planarity. This matters when interpreting molecular structures and distinguishing a planar alkene unit from a non-planar saturated ring.
9701-13.3.4.note:
- Planar: the atoms under discussion lie in the same plane.
- All six atoms of ethene are planar.
- A saturated cyclohexane ring normally puckers and is non-planar.
- A flat paper diagram does not prove planarity.
9701-13.3.4.self_explain: Why does a flat hexagon drawing fail to show the actual three-dimensional shape of cyclohexane?

options.A: Only its two carbon atoms are planar
options.B: All six atoms lie in one plane

discover.explanation: The sp² carbon centres and their attached hydrogen atoms share one plane; the p orbitals form a π bond above and below it.
